papers.title: SADET: Efficient active suspension control for intensive care ambulances via self-attention and deterministic experience tracking
papers.authors: He X., Liu J., Meng Y., Lin H.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional vibration control in intensive care ambulances demands algorithms that are simultaneously high-performance and lightweight for real-world deployment. This study proposes the SADET algorithm, which integrates a Self-Attention (SA) mechanism with Deterministic Experience Tracking (DET) within an asymmetric strong Critic and weak Actor architecture. Built upon a 7-DOF ambulance dynamics model and a domain-randomization training protocol over ISO 8608 random road profiles, the SA-enhanced Critic enables an extremely lightweight Actor, with the derived SADET-n requiring only 124 parameters, representing a 99.9 % reduction from the DET baseline. Experimental results demonstrate that the top-performing SADET-x variant achieves vertical vibration suppression improvements of 62.9 %, 56.4 %, and 11.0 % over DDPG, TD3, and DET respectively, while reducing the root mean square values of roll and pitch accelerations by 75.4 % and 56.5 %. Generalization studies on 400 unseen road profiles spanning Classes A through D, vehicle speeds from 10 to 50 m/s, and sprung mass variations of ±500 kg confirm robust cross-scenario adaptability, and dedicated fault-injection tests further verify that performance is sustained under sensor noise and intermittent data loss representative of production automotive sensor networks. Comparative power analysis additionally shows that SADET delivers state-of-the-art comfort improvement at an actuator power consumption no higher than that of substantially less effective baselines. The present work establishes a deployable lightweight framework for the application of deep reinforcement learning to complex real-world control systems and provides a meaningful advance in the safety and comfort of medical transportation.

papers.title: Disentangling generative chaos: A multi-scale hypergraph diffusion framework for interpretable recommendation
papers.authors: Tuo S., Geng J., Chen S., Qiu K., Luo Z.
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation often suffers from “generative chaos”—a disordered and entangled latent state that degrades ranking accuracy and interpretability. To address this challenge, we propose Dis-Rec, a framework that pioneers a “structure-guided generation” paradigm. Dis-Rec operates through three synergistic components: (1) utilizing a latent diffusion model to construct a high-fidelity user preference manifold, providing a robust informational foundation; (2) introducing a multi-scale hypergraph strategy to concurrently encode short-term sequential contexts and long-term interest patterns into a unified structural prior; and (3) devising a disentangled gating decoder that exploits these topological priors to steer the automatic decomposition of chaotic latent vectors into semantically orthogonal intent channels, enabling context-aware adaptive fusion via a dynamic gating mechanism. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate significant performance gains. Notably, compared with the strongest baseline, Dis-Rec achieves a 7.67% relative improvement in NDCG@10 on ML-1 M and a 4.24% Recall gain on the sparse Toys dataset, effectively overcoming the data scarcity bottleneck typical of generative models. These results verify the critical role of structured disentanglement in enhancing the robustness of generative recommendation.

papers.title: TemFRC: Enterprise financial risk prediction with temporal folding and risk contrast
papers.authors: Wang M., Huang W., Xie W., Hou J., Gao X., Fu X.
papers.abstract: AbstractEnterprise financial risk prediction constitutes a critical component of contemporary corporate governance, profoundly impacting an organization’s capacity for risk mitigation and data-driven decision-making. However, existing methods that treat financial data as a time series mostly focus on capturing trend variations, while ignoring the fact that enterprise development often exhibits periodic patterns and inter-enterprise similarities, resulting in limited model capacity to learn financial characteristics. To address this issue, we propose TemFRC, a novel method for enterprise financial risk prediction that enhances model performance by capturing various periodic patterns in financial data and leveraging risk similarity among enterprises. Specifically, TemFRC consists of two core modules: the temporal folding module and the risk contrast module. The temporal folding module transforms one-dimensional time series into two-dimensional temporal feature maps, enabling more comprehensive capture of trend variations and periodic patterns in financial data. The risk contrast module optimizes enterprise feature representations within the embedding space via contrastive learning, thereby facilitating the modeling of inter-enterprise risk similarities. Finally, the feature representations learned through the two modules are leveraged to determine whether a company is at risk of financial distress. Experiments are conducted on a real-world financial statement dataset comprising 3622 listed companies. The results demonstrate that TemFRC achieves state-of-the-art prediction performance, reaching a Macro-F1 score of 0.8753, which represents a 2.87% improvement over the best-performing baseline model.

papers.title: Diffusion-based generative modeling for expert team formation
papers.authors: Saliminabi M.H., Ebrahimi S., Hamidi Rad R., Androutsos D., Zarrinkalam F., Bagheri E.
papers.abstract: Forming effective expert teams is central to domains where solving complex problems requires diverse, complementary skills. However, automating this task is highly challenging due to sparse co-occurrence data, long-tailed expert participation, and the combinatorial complexity of unseen skill configurations. Existing graph-based, probabilistic, and neural approaches often struggle with generalization, fairness, and robustness, leading to biased selections that favor historically popular experts over more suitable candidates. To address these challenges, we propose a generative framework for expert team formation based on denoising diffusion probabilistic models. We cast team formation as skill-conditioned imputation (i.e., inpainting), where skills are treated as observed context and the expert component is generated via conditional diffusion sampling. This design enables our method to preserve semantic skill–expert alignment, mitigate data sparsity, and generate diverse yet contextually coherent teams. Extensive experiments on DBLP and DOTA2 datasets show that our model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving over 3× higher recall (16.4% vs. 5.0%) and MAP (9.7% vs. 2.2%) on DBLP, while delivering more than 5× improvement in MRR (13.3% vs. 2.5%) on DOTA2. Fairness analysis further demonstrates that our method reduces average overlap with the top-100 most popular experts to 2.6, compared to 86.7 for the strongest baseline, and achieves near-optimal diversity with NDKL ≈ 0.1 under high non-popular expert ratios.For reproducibility purposes, we made our code and model publicly available at https://github.com/17shiraz/DiffTF.

papers.title: Structure-aware multi-teacher distillation for noise node classification
papers.authors: Hu B., Wen G., Huang Y., Liu Y., Zhu X.
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation methods are very popular for solving the issue of noise node classification (NNC). However, these methods often fail to consider the structural information in graph data or output uncorrected prediction labels in the teacher models due to the influence of noise labels, resulting in degraded generalization performance for constructing a teacher–student training framework in the Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). To effectively address this challenge, we propose a new method named Structure-Aware Multi-Teacher Distillation (SAMTD) for noise node classification. Specifically, we first train multiple teacher models to ensure diversity. We then propose an embedding structure consistency distillation method to make the student model capture the rich structural information encoded in the teachers’ embeddings, as well as a prediction consistency weighting strategy to guide the student model to focus more on the reliable classification knowledge provided by the teacher models. Finally, we introduce a label enhancement module to continuously improve the overall label quality in the dataset. Experimental results on five real-world datasets under five different noise settings demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in classification accuracy, achieving an average improvement of 1.2%. The source code is at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SAMTD.

papers.title: An LLM-based NLP pipeline to assist government agencies in digesting massive public comments and mitigating spam
papers.authors: Dong W., Zhu R., Jensen M., Bessarabova E., Sachdeva S., Kim J.N., Talbert N., Perez L.A., Li Y.
papers.abstract: Public comments are a crucial resource for regulatory agencies in policy-making. However, large-scale comment analysis is labor-intensive and heavily distorted by spam. While large language models (LLMs) present a promising solution, real-world deployments face critical challenges, including spam-biased topic distribution and argument-extraction errors. Moreover, several agencies we interviewed treat data privacy as one of their top priorities, hence restricting the use of cloud-based LLMs. Meanwhile, the effectiveness of privacy-preserving local models remains underexplored in rule-making. This study aims to develop a unified LLM-based summarization pipeline that jointly quantifies spam volume, detects spam templates, and enables argument-aware summarization, while remaining deployable under real-world privacy constraints. We conduct experiments on three public comment datasets drawn from the Federal Communications Commission, the Forest Service, and the Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division in collaboration with communication experts and government staff. The results reveal that the proposed pipeline achieves promising performance on quantifying spam volume, with an F1 score of 0.987, 0.993, and 0.995. The pipeline further addresses spam template detection, consistently achieving a high BERTScore when compared with expert-defined ground-truth templates. We also evaluate the pipeline’s performance on argument-aware summarization, finding that few-shot prompting notably outperforms its zero-shot counterparts. When implemented locally in Llama, a much smaller version of the LLM, the pipeline performed comparably to GPT-4, the state-of-the-art cloud-based LLM. This work enables regulatory agencies to efficiently distill public opinions from large-scale comment datasets, providing structured, argument-aware summaries that inform evidence-based policy rule-making.

papers.title: MSTDF-AD: Modeling spatiotemporal dependency fusion for non-stationary time series anomaly detection
papers.authors: Shi W., Xiao H., Qiu Z., Zeng Z., Zhu W., Zhang S., Xiao R.
papers.abstract: Existing time series anomaly detection methods often rely on stationarity assumptions, struggling with real-world non-stationary factors, such as trend shifts and seasonal fluctuations, which result in high false alarms, missed detections, and inadequate spatiotemporal modeling. This paper proposes a novel modeling spatiotemporal dependency fusion for non-stationary time series anomaly detection (MSTDF-AD), featuring three key innovations: (1) Spatiotemporal fusion decomposition: Jointly models complex dependencies while extracting stable components; (2) Multiscale feature fusion: Integrates cross-scale information to enhance local–global anomaly perception; (3) Dynamic KL divergence weight: Using simulated annealing to adaptively optimize VAE training, mitigating posterior collapse. Evaluated on five real-world datasets, industrial control (SWaT), cloud services (PSM), hardware maintenance (SMD), and aerospace monitoring (MSL/SMAP), MSTDF-AD achieves a 96.47% average F1-score, outperforming 19 baseline methods (e.g., +2.58% over GDCMAD, +0.21% over MtsCID), with exceptional performance in hardware fault detection (SMD: 93.94%) and spacecraft telemetry (SMAP: 97.85%), validating its effectiveness in anomaly detection tasks. The code is available at https://github.com/Conviss/MSTDF-AD.

papers.title: Dynamic knowledge landscape construction for AI-driven emergency decision-making: An STM-LLM framework with triple-LLM synergistic labeling
papers.authors: He K., Wu J., Wang C.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance emergency decision-making, but systematic reviews of its knowledge evolution remain lacking. Based on 525 papers on AI-driven emergency decision-making (AI-EDM) from Web of Science (2020–2025), this study proposes an STM-LLM framework integrating Structural Topic Modeling (STM) and Large Language Models (LLMs), and develops a Triple-LLM Synergistic Labeling (TLS) mechanism for automated and bias-resistant topic labeling generation. To validate the efficacy of the framework, systematic comparative and ablation experiments were designed. The application of the framework in the field of AI-EDM facilitates the identification of research topics, followed by analysis of their spatiotemporal distribution and evolution. A Logistic-Normal Generalized Linear Model (GLM) quantified the effects of five covariates on topic prevalence, and a three-dimensional strategic map identified research frontiers and gaps. The experimental results show that the STM-LLM framework significantly outperforms mainstream baseline methods in both topic label quality and generation efficiency, and the TLS mechanism effectively improves labeling stability. The study identified nine stable topics in the AI-EDM domain that show a “growth-consolidation-decline” pattern. Research funding showed a positive correlation with the development of human–AI collaborative platforms ((Formula presented) ), and differences in research focus were observed between Chinese and international scholars. None of the topics demonstrated significant preferences in terms of collaboration type. Both human intervention and type of decision objective demonstrated distinct patterns of association with different topics. Furthermore, Topics are categorized into four types—Leading, Emerging, Receding, and Persistent. Based on these findings, we further propose a “problem–technology–benefit” framework to systematically support domain advancement. The STM-LLM framework automates dynamic knowledge landscape construction, overcoming manual topic labeling limitations and offering data-driven methodological and practical support for AI-EDM research.

papers.title: S2RAF: A Semantic and Structure aware ReAsoning Framework for question answering over textual graphs
papers.authors: Luo J., Hu P., Zhang M.
papers.abstract: Textual graph question answering (Graph QA) aims to answer natural language queries by reasoning over graphs with textual attributes. Existing methods typically introduce secondary or noisy information when retrieving question-relevant subgraphs. Moreover, the information gap between graph structure and semantics often results in information loss, negatively impacting model performance. In this paper, we propose a Semantic and Structure aware ReAsoning Framework (S2RAF), which integrates structural and semantic information for precise retrieval of relevant facts and high-quality injection of reasoning knowledge. Specifically, we first develop a question-guided retrieval mechanism to dynamically adjust node weights for the adaptive extraction of targeted subgraphs. Then, a dual-level optimization strategy is introduced, combining an LLM-based reasoning scorer with a similarity-based semantic scorer to jointly optimize the subgraphs, effectively denoising and focusing on critical facts. Finally, we propose G-Adapter, which dynamically injects graph information into LLMs, achieving graph-text fusion and enhancing reasoning ability over graphs. Extensive experiments on four Graph QA datasets demonstrate that S2RAF successfully achieves competitive performance. Particularly, S2RAF outperforms existing methods by 5.63%, 5.36%, and 23.83% on ExplaGraphs, SceneGraphs, and CWQ datasets, respectively, confirming the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed model.

papers.title: Large language models for business and management applications: A review
papers.authors: Arslan M., Munawar S., Riaz Z., Cruz C.
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping business and management, yet existing reviews remain fragmented, with limited integration of bibliometric structure and operational insights. This study addresses that gap by combining bibliometric analysis with a systematic thematic synthesis, linking publication trends, intellectual structure, and real-world deployment patterns across 84 application-focused studies selected from an initial pool of 210 records identified from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (up to August 2025). The analysis shows a sharp post-2023 expansion of research alongside a shift from general-purpose conversational use toward domain-specific and architecture-aware implementations. In contrast to prior reviews, this study identifies how application patterns differ across domains: knowledge-intensive contexts increasingly adopt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for grounding, while finance applications more frequently rely on fine-tuned and domain-specific models. Keyword co-occurrence analysis highlights a technology-centric core, dominated by ChatGPT, foundation models, and RAG, linked to key business domains including operations, finance, marketing, and supply chain management. While organisations are increasingly adopting customised LLM pipelines and governance-aware workflows, challenges persist in accuracy, integration, ethical risk, and data quality. By consolidating dispersed evidence, this study offers a structured understanding of emerging application patterns and provides guidance for future research and responsible enterprise adoption of LLMs.

papers.title: Exploring contextual and pairwise semantic-enhanced embedding with adaptive fusion for knowledge graph completion
papers.authors: Xue Z., Chen J., Hu X., Lin Z.
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims to predict missing facts by embedding entities and relations, emerging as the predominant method for intelligent reasoning. However, existing KGC approaches tend to ignore the potential noise and uncertainty, as the contribution of each connected relation to entities varies across distinct link scenarios. Moreover, the simple aggregation process during embedding learning struggles to capture both global and local information simultaneously. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes the Adaptive Contextual-Pairwise Network (AdaCPN) model. Specifically, hybrid-granularity semantic augmentation derives a contextual representation of triplets by attending to the surrounding feature information, and suppressing redundant semantic information. Furthermore, it boosts predictive semantics with pairwise frequency weights of triplets, achieving dynamic contribution allocation and alleviating semantic distribution disparity. Additionally, AdaCPN utilizes adaptive convolution kernels of distinct sizes to broaden the receptive field, which fuses global and detailed features during the aggregation process. AdaCPN is validated on nine benchmark datasets, containing millions of triplets. Experimental results confirm that in MRR on FB15k-237 and WN18RR, AdaCPN not only outperforms neural network-based SOTA methods with improvements of 5.8% and 3.4% (0.430 vs. 0.372, 0.551 vs. 0.517), but also improves by 3.8% and 0.2% (0.430 vs. 0.392, 0.551 vs. 0.549) compared to LLM-based SOTA approaches.

papers.title: Semi-COPRA: An overlapping community-aware model for multi-dimensional opinion dynamics and consensus analysis
papers.authors: Zhao Y., Mao H., Dong J., Hu J.
papers.abstract: The evolution of group opinions in social networks is fundamentally shaped by community structure, particularly in networks with overlapping communities and multi-dimensional opinions. In this study, we propose Semi-COPRA, an overlapping community detection algorithm that combines a semi-asynchronous label update mechanism with a dynamic threshold strategy to mitigate sensitivity to random initialization. Experiments on four real-world networks demonstrate that Semi-COPRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, yielding average improvements of 81% in EQ, 15% in F1 score, and 27% in ONMI over the original COPRA. Building on the detected overlapping communities, we further develop a multi-dimensional opinion dynamics model incorporating a community-aware trust function and a topic interdependence matrix. Simulation results show that increasing community overlap enhances inter-group consensus while weakening intra-group cohesion. In addition, moderate topic interdependence accelerates convergence across opinion dimensions, facilitating the formation of global consensus. These findings establish a structurally integrated modeling framework that links overlapping community detection with multi-dimensional opinion evolution, providing new insights into information diffusion and opinion regulation in complex social systems.

papers.title: A hierarchical RL model for Chinese medical NER with radical semantics and dynamic decision
papers.authors: Ruan G., Xia L.
papers.abstract: To address key challenges in Chinese medical Named Entity Recognition (NER)-such as ambiguous entity boundaries, poor generalization of low-frequency entities, and the difficulty of integrating external knowledge-we propose a novel model that integrates radical semantics with hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL). First, we design an adaptive gating mechanism that fuses radical features (e.g., “疒” for diseases) with MacBERT embeddings to enhance semantic representation. Second, a decoupled HRL framework decomposes NER into boundary detection (Actor-Boundary) and type classification (Actor-Type), optimizing nested entity recognition via dynamic rewards. Third, a lightweight BiGRU-Transformer architecture with dynamic CRF decoding reduces computational costs. Evaluated on the CCKS2019 dataset (1,379 annotated samples), our model achieves a 92.51% F1-score-outperforming BERT-BiLSTM-CRF-based baselines. Robustness is validated on CMeEE, IMCS, and DiaKG datasets, providing a transferable solution for electronic medical record structuring.

papers.title: Modelling implicit bias in gender–career associations: A systematic comparison of language models
papers.authors: Porshnev A., Kiy K.D., O'Donoghue D., Singh M., Wingfield C., Lynott D.
papers.abstract: Biases in language and their reflection in language models have attracted researchers' attention, particularly with the growth of large language models (LLMs). However, many questions on the links between language models and people’s biased attitudes remain unanswered. In the current preregistered study, we focus on gender–career bias to examine the extent to which language models can be used to model behavioural responses in the Gender–Career Implicit Association Test (IAT). We provide a systematic evaluation of a range of language models, including n-gram, count vector, predict (word2vec), and Large Language Models (LLMs), to determine how well they capture people’s behaviour in the IAT. We compared response time data from over 800,000 participants from the UK and US against 25 language models, with a total of 675 model variants. We find that many language models, including large language models (LLMs), correlated well with human behavior. While results support previous findings for both predict and count model families, we observed that performance of LLMs was consistently different from that of simpler predict models, frequently exhibiting correlations in the opposite direction. Thus, our findings reinforce the idea that societal biases are generally encoded in language, but that large language models can exhibit behaviors different to classical language models. Study preregistration, code, and materials are all available from the project website https://osf.io/n36gr?.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of Artificial Intelligence in Qur’anic research: Trends, methods, challenges, and future directions
papers.authors: Al-Azani S., Abudalfa S., Samma H.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a transformative tool in the Holy Qur’an domain, supporting diverse tasks including recitation accuracy assessment (e.g., Tajweed rule detection), semantic exegesis (e.g., contextual retrieval of Tafsir), verse classification (e.g., identifying rulings or themes), and memorization support (e.g., providing feedback on recitation accuracy). However, applying AI in the domain of the Holy Qur’an requires prioritizing religious principles and ensuring a high level of accuracy in accordance with those principles. This study provides a comprehensive review of the role of AI in Qur’anic research, based on an analysis of 151 core studies. These studies have been systematically analyzed and evaluated using a well-defined set of evaluation criteria. It is structured around six thematic axes: trends, tasks, techniques, resources, challenges, and ethical concerns, each formulated as a distinct research question. This article also develops several taxonomies and classifications, providing a structured framework for researchers and practitioners to navigate the complexities of applying AI in Qur’anic research. The first taxonomy, a generic taxonomy, highlights key tasks, approaches, modalities, resources, subjects, and languages, offering a comprehensive overview of the field. Another classification focuses on the AI techniques applied in this domain, including machine/deep learning, NLP, speech recognition, computer vision, and ontology-, rule-, and semantic-based approaches. A further taxonomy is developed to address the challenges in this field, categorizing them into Qur’anic-related, computational processing, Arabic NLP-related, limitations of resources, and ethical and religious considerations. It also provides a critical analysis of current approaches in the field, identifies key limitations, and recommends future research directions to enhance progress and address existing challenges. Ultimately, this research serves as a thorough guide, deepening the understanding of the AI landscape in the field and offering valuable insights for developing reliable, advanced, and sensitive AI techniques.

papers.title: Mind perception of artificial intelligence: A systematic review
papers.authors: Li Y., Qin X., Yam K.C., Gray K., Cheng X., Wen J., Lai X.
papers.abstract: Mind perception shapes human-AI interaction, yet there is a lack of comprehensive review for understanding the antecedents and outcomes of the mind perception of AI. This review analyzes 153 empirical studies from the past 20 years and synthesizes the key antecedents and outcomes of the mind perception of AI. We first identify human-related antecedents (e.g., demographics, personality traits, psychological conditions), AI-related factors (e.g., humanlike appearance, transparency, social identity cues, functions), and interaction-related factors (e.g., how humans interact with AI, how AI responds, interaction outcomes) that shape perceptions of AI’s agency and experience. These perceptions of AI’s agency and experience lead to cognitive, emotional, attitudinal, and behavioral consequences that are different from human-human interactions. By comparing findings across the dimensions of agency and experience, we offer nuanced insights into how people perceive AI’s mind and how these perceptions affect human-AI interactions. Finally, we suggest promising avenues for future research.

papers.title: PAGSL: Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning for explainable scholar recommendation
papers.authors: Xu J., Ai M., Huang J., Jia T.
papers.abstract: Explainable scholar recommendation aims to identify potential scholars of interest and provide reasonable explanations for the recommendations. However, existing frameworks struggle with optimization-induced noise and ”hub node bias”, yielding trivial explanations that lack hierarchical depth and personalization. To this end, we propose a novel explainable scholar recommendation model, Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning (named PAGSL). PAGSL combines representation learning and semantic path knowledge to ensure recommendation performance while providing interpretable results from two perspectives. Specifically, it activates latent academic paths among entities through graph augmentation and employs a path-based neural network to encode these paths for recommendation. A masking mechanism with path score optimization is designed to generate concise and informative explanations. We evaluate PAGSL on three academic datasets (Scholat, AMiner, and ResearchGate), comprising approximately 49,000 authors and over 330,000 interaction records. Experimental evaluations validate that PAGSL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant improvements of 6.31% in F1-score, 6.29% in Accuracy and 5.95% in AUC for recommendation. Crucially, in terms of explainability, we provide quantitative results and visualization effects. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our heterogeneous convolution and path representation learning. PAGSL achieves strong performance in both recommendation accuracy and explainability.

papers.title: DiaCOLQ: A benchmark for Chinese offensive language quadruple prediction in multi-turn dialogues
papers.authors: Wang Y., Zhang S., Zhou Z., Zhang L., Bai J., Lu J., Fan B., Bu F.
papers.abstract: Warning: This paper contains offensive language that may cause discomfort for readers.Structured analysis of offensive language in multi-speaker dialogues remains underexplored in Chinese, where expressions are often implicit, context-dependent, and spread across multiple turns. Prior research has primarily focused on sentence-based classification, lacking the ability to model the dynamic, interactive nature of real-world offensive discourse. In this paper, we propose the task of Chinese Offensive Language Quadruple Prediction in multi-turn dialogues, which aims to extract structured quadruples identifying the target, argument, category and speaker within dialogue contexts. To support this task, we construct DiaCOLQ, the first Chinese dialogue-based dataset for offensive language understanding, comprising 6401 utterances and 3854 annotated offensive quadruples. The dataset preserves reply-thread structures and incorporates coreference resolution to unify cross-turn references, enhancing its capacity for fine-grained semantic representation. We evaluate several vanilla and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) on DiaCOLQ. Results show that while vanilla LLMs can detect explicit offenses, fine-tuned LLMs significantly improve quadruple consistency and semantic alignment, with Hard-F1 and Soft-F1 increasing by 6.15% and 5.23%, respectively.

papers.title: A gated multi-scale attention framework for automated short answer grading in Turkish
papers.authors: Kaya M., Kavun M.
papers.abstract: This study proposes a new deep learning architecture for automated short-answer grading (ASAG) in Turkish. The model integrates transformer-based encoders (BERTurk, RoBERTa-Turkish (RoBERTa), ELECTRA-Turkish (ELECTRA)) with a Gated Multi-Scale Head Attention (GMHA) layer. Additionally, a BiLSTM network and parallel CNN layers are employed to capture both global dependencies and local linguistic patterns.The model was evaluated on a newly created Turkish dataset containing 2200 student responses from 220 learners, each graded by four experts. Among the pretrained Turkish encoders, the BERT-based model with GMHA achieved the best performance (QWK = 0.839, Pearson = 0.856, RMSE = 0.918). The model was also compared with traditional machine learning approaches and large language models (LLMs) using the Leave-One-Question-Out (LOQO) validation protocol. Under this setting, it achieved QWK = 0.337, Pearson = 0.468, and RMSE = 1.213, outperforming all baselines.Ablation studies confirmed the effectiveness of the GMHA and parallel CNN components. These results highlight both the theoretical contribution of multi-scale gated attention and the practical potential of developing reliable automated grading systems for morphologically rich, low-resource languages like Turkish.

papers.title: Cross-platform evaluation of reasoning capabilities in foundation models
papers.authors: de Curtò J., de Zarzà I., García P., Cabot J., Cano J.C., Calafate C.T.
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive cross-platform evaluation of reasoning capabilities in contemporary foundation models, establishing an infrastructure-agnostic benchmark across three computational paradigms: HPC supercomputing (MareNostrum 5), cloud platforms (Nebius AI Studio), and university clusters (a node with eight H200 GPUs). We evaluate 15 foundation models across 79 problems spanning eight academic domains (Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology, Statistics, Calculus, and Optimization) through three experimental phases: (1) Baseline establishment: Six models (Mixtral-8x7B, Phi-3, LLaMA 3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9b, Mistral-7B, OLMo-7B) evaluated on 19 problems using MareNostrum 5, establishing methodology and reference performance; (2) Infrastructure validation: The 19-problem benchmark repeated on university cluster (seven models including Falcon-Mamba state-space architecture) and Nebius AI Studio (nine state-of-the-art models: Hermes-4 70B/405B, LLaMA 3.1-405B/3.3-70B, Qwen3 30B/235B, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-OSS 20B/120B) to confirm infrastructure-agnostic reproducibility; (3) Extended evaluation: Full 79-problem assessment on both university cluster and Nebius platforms, probing generalization at scale across architectural diversity. Results challenge prevailing scaling assumptions through a parameter efficiency paradox: Hermes-4-70B (70B parameters) achieves the highest score among extended models (0.598), outperforming both its 405B counterpart (0.573) and Meta’s LLaMA 3.1-405B (0.560). Domain-specific analysis reveals LLaMA 3.1-405B achieves record Calculus performance (0.717), while DeepSeek-R1 sets unprecedented standards for reasoning transparency (0.716 step-accuracy). Qwen3 models demonstrate exceptional consistency, with mean per-evaluation standard deviation of 0.013, the lowest among Nebius models. The findings challenge conventional scaling assumptions, establish training data quality as more critical than model size, and provide actionable guidelines for model selection across educational, production, and research contexts. The tri-infrastructure methodology and 79-problem benchmark enable longitudinal tracking of reasoning capabilities as foundation models evolve.

papers.title: Wavelet transform-based versatile watermarking for facial manipulation source tracing and detection
papers.authors: Zhang Y., Lin W., Xu J., Shi L., Xu W., Xu Y., Kou F.
papers.abstract: Malicious facial manipulation poses a critical challenge to digital forensics, as existing passive and proactive methods struggle to achieve reliable source tracing and facial manipulation detection. We propose a novel wavelet transform-based versatile watermarking method, WavMark, to address the above challenges. First, WavMark combines the semi-fragile image watermark with the robust bit watermark, integrating watermark embedding and extraction into an end-to-end framework. Second, we propose a WGFB with an ADSF strategy, which enhances the detection capability of the semi-fragile image watermark by decomposing and fusing the low-frequency and high-frequency components of the original and watermarked images. In addition, we introduce the Bit Encoder for embedding bit information and enhancing the robustness of the bit watermark against facial manipulation attacks. Finally, we propose a PGAL strategy within the random noise manipulation pool, which enables automatic sample label assignment without requiring pre-labeled data. Comprehensive experiments on CelebA-HQ demonstrate that WavMark significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art forensics approaches, achieving 91.11% BCR and 100% AUC in the cross-manipulation source tracing and facial manipulation detection scenario at the resolution of 256 × 256. The results verify that WavMark effectively unifies robust source tracing and reliable facial manipulation detection, providing a scalable and imperceptible proactive forensic solution for real-world applications.

papers.title: Q-RUN: Quantum-inspired data re-uploading networks
papers.authors: Qiao W., Wang S., Zhang P., Ming Y., Zhao J.
papers.abstract: AbstractData re-uploading quantum circuits (DRQC) offer better expressiveness than feed-forward neural networks, but their practical use is constrained by the current development of quantum hardware. We propose a quantum-inspired data re-uploading network (Q-RUN), which approximately captures the Fourier-expressive advantages of DRQC without relying on any quantum resources. We conducted comprehensive evaluations of Q-RUN on seven representative tasks covering both data modeling and prediction. Compared with state-of-the-art neural layers, Q-RUN achieves simultaneous reductions in both test error and learnable parameters. For example, in molecular energy modeling, Q-RUN reduces modeling error by 91.16% while using 23.25% fewer parameters. Moreover, Q-RUN is designed as a modular layer that may serve as an alternative to fully connected layers, with potential performance benefits across different architectures. For instance, applying Q-RUN in large language model fine-tuning improves accuracy by 1.02%. These results demonstrate that principles from quantum machine learning can inspire the design of more expressive and parameter-efficient classical neural network layers.

papers.title: Catching fraudulent “invisible hands”: An approach to finding associative dense blocks in bipartite graphs
papers.authors: Ren Y., Lin H., Yu J., Feng Z., Zhou J., Man L., Liu M., Liu G.
papers.abstract: Frauds always trail with humans as shadows through a variety of channels, leading to severe social and economic damage. In cyberspace, fraudsters often act in coordinated groups, while higher-level actors operate as low-intensity “invisible hands” spanning multiple groups. In this paper, we formalize a novel group-fraud structure on bipartite graphs, termed Associative Dense Blocks (ADB), consisting of several dense subgraphs linked by associative (bridging) nodes. To quantify such anomalous structures, we introduce the Association Score (AS) as the optimization objective, and propose a greedy algorithm, SMEA, to maximize the objective for ADB detection. We also propose SMEAr, a similarity-based variant that reduces redundant re-evaluations during node merging. This variant substantially reduces computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Meanwhile, through theoretical analysis of a generated random graph, we derive a lower bound on the approximation quality of the proposed algorithms for recovering ADB structures. Extensive experiments on synthetic bipartite graphs demonstrate the effectiveness and adaptivity of the proposed methods, achieving improvements of up to 39.3% on Jaccard similarity over the state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, group fraud detection analysis on a large real-world telecom network with 124,680 calling records presents its practical utility in identifying fraudulent “invisible hands”.

papers.title: Hypergraph Kolmogorov–Arnold networks contrastive hashing for unsupervised cross-modal retrieval
papers.authors: Yang Z., Wang B., Long W., Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Cross-modal hashing has become a prominent research focus due to its ability to achieve efficient information retrieval, high-speed query performance, and minimal storage overhead, making it indispensable for processing complex multimedia datasets in academic and industrial applications. However, existing methods suffer from three intertwined challenges: limited nonlinear fitting capacity due to fixed-architecture networks (e.g., MLPs), which struggle to model complex cross-modal semantics; inability to capture beyond-pairwise correlations as they often rely on simple graphs, thus failing to preserve fine-grained structural information; and sensitivity to false-negative pairs in unsupervised contrastive learning, which severely degrades retrieval accuracy. To systematically tackle these challenges, we propose Hyper-KAN Contrastive Hashing (HKCH), an unsupervised framework that introduces three key architectural innovations: first, we redesign the feature mapping module by replacing traditional MLPs with Fast-Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (F-KANs) employing learnable spline-RBF activation functions, enabling dynamic and expressive nonlinear semantic representation; second, we incorporate hypergraph neural networks to model higher-order associations within and across modalities, effectively capturing multi-way structural correlations while filtering semantic redundancy; third, we develop a novel contrastive hashing module with adaptive weights and an improved ternary loss to robustly mitigate false-negative interference and enhance semantic alignment. These components are not merely combined but are structurally integrated into a coherent architecture that advances beyond existing approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that HKCH achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with average accuracy gains of 1.38% on MIRFlickr, 1.72% on NUS-WIDE, and 1.37% on MSCOCO significant margins that validate its architectural effectiveness.

papers.title: From latent structures to explicit reasoning: Synergizing clustering and LLM for explainable and robust rumor detection
papers.authors: Zhou X., Tong N., Wang D., Li F.
papers.abstract: Misinformation disseminated on social media poses a systemic risk to the global information environment. Existing detection models encounter a transparency robustness bottleneck, while Large Language Models (LLMs) suffer from ungrounded hallucinations. To address these deficiencies, we propose Topic-Aware Chain-of-Reasoning (TA-CoR), a dual process framework synergizing unsupervised structure distillation with symbolic inference. To instantiate native explainability, the Hierarchical Topic Residual Refinement (HTRR) mechanism distills latent discourse into multi granular thematic priors, acting as semantic guardrails that guide grounded LLM reasoning. Systemic robustness is reinforced through a Semantic Adversarial Training (L-SAT) regimen, which utilizes meaning preserving reformulations to cultivate adversarial cognitive alignment, forcing the model to discern the invariant mendacious core of misinformation. Evaluations on Twitter15, Twitter16, and PHEME demonstrate that TA-CoR achieves state-of-the-art accuracies (80.89%, 82.97%, and 77.34%). Notably, the framework exhibits superior resilience within less than a 15% drop in performance under attacks and human evaluation confirms high rationale fidelity (>[jls-end-space/]4.6/5.0). This work transitions rumor detection from opaque pattern matching to a transparent and reasoning method grounded on evidence.

papers.title: DiPaNet: Discriminative Pattern-aware Network for Multivariate Time Series Classification
papers.authors: Xiao Z., Hu J., Luo C., Chen X., Wang Y.
papers.abstract: The core objective of multivariate time series classification is to identify temporal-wise and variable-wise discriminative patterns. Previous methods either focus solely on temporal features within individual variables or have limited capacity to model interactions among variables, particularly when capturing short-term patterns (locality) and delayed responses among variables (asynchrony). To address these limitations, we propose a novel method, Discriminative Pattern-aware Network for Multivariate Time Series Classification (DiPaNet), which jointly models discriminative patterns along both the temporal and variable dimensions. Along the temporal dimension, the multivariate time series is divided into local segments, and a temporal convolutional structure is employed to extract temporal-wise discriminative patterns. Along the variable dimension, a Variable Interaction Pattern Detection Module is introduced to capture variable-wise discriminative patterns. In this module, the graph construction step represents each variable within a segment as a node in a graph. The Pattern-based Graph Neural Network incorporates the pattern-based adjacency matrices into the message-passing process and employs pattern fusion to combine node features derived from different patterns, thereby enhancing the model’s sensitivity to critical interaction structures. Experiments on 22 UEA datasets demonstrate that DiPaNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 1.8%.

papers.title: Forecasting secondary risks in emergencies: A transferable early warning framework using event logic graphs from social media
papers.authors: Li S., Tian C., Du X., Li Y.
papers.abstract: Social media has become a critical arena for public opinion during emergencies, where the rapid evolution of events can generate unforeseen secondary risks. This study develops and validates a transferable early warning framework that applies Event Logic Graphs (ELGs) to move beyond retrospective analysis, toward proactive risk forecasting. First, this study proposes a novel hybrid Rule-Large Language Model framework to extract events and multiple types of logical relations from noisy social media data. Second, a comparative analysis is conducted by constructing separate ELGs for each event: a natural disaster and public health crisis. Finally, regarding the historical ELG as the knowledge base, the framework incorporates the event chain similarity calculations with context-aware filtering and sentiment enhanced re-ranking mechanism. Specifically, this mechanism ensures prediction validity by filtering context mismatched risks and capturing verified public sentiment to prioritize potential threats. The results present that the hybrid framework significantly outperforms the pure rule-based model in logic triples extraction. The analysis reveals that emergencies evolve into two different structural prototypes: natural disaster is manifested as “linear cascade” models, and public health crisis shows “cyclic feedback loop” characteristics, which provides a new computational perspective for agenda setting theory. In addition, the cross-event secondary risk prediction framework achieves satisfactory predictive performance across Top-3, 5, and 10 cutoffs, demonstrating that integrating context constraints and, more critically, credibility weighted sentiment analysis, achieves the most substantial improvement in identifying high-priority risks. This research contributes to the literature by proposing a robust method for building ELG with multiple logical relationships, helping emergency management shift from passive monitoring to active risk prevention and control.

papers.title: Opinion importance analysis with single-review representation for enhanced restaurant selection decision-making
papers.authors: Chen Z., Chai N., Liang R., Deng M., Wang X., Wang J.
papers.abstract: Online restaurant reviews often express multiple viewpoints within a single review, yet existing studies predominantly focus on aggregated representations at the restaurant level and rarely model the relative importance of opinions at the single-review level. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel opinion importance analysis model that jointly considers content semantics and sentiment characteristics to estimate the relative importance of viewpoints expressed within a single review. Building on this, we develop a single-review level opinion representation framework, together with an opinion completion strategy that infers missing viewpoints based on neighboring reviews, and an importance-aware aggregation mechanism for integrating information across reviews. Experiments on a real-world Yelp dataset comprising 31,412 reviews from 10 restaurants extract six key themes using a combined topic model. Empirical analysis shows that multi-theme opinion expression within individual reviews is prevalent, with approximately 56%–86% of reviews containing viewpoints across multiple themes, while a substantial portion of theme-level opinions remains unobserved within individual reviews. The proposed opinion completion strategy effectively recovers these missing viewpoints, enabling more comprehensive review representations. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that explicitly modeling opinion importance and completing missing viewpoints yield more informative review representations than existing alternatives. Sensitivity analysis further confirms the robustness of the proposed framework with respect to key parameters. This work provides a novel paradigm for review analysis, shifting from coarse-grained aggregation at the restaurant level to fine-grained, single-review opinion modeling that captures both opinion importance and missing viewpoints, with important implications for advanced opinion mining and personalized recommendation systems.

papers.title: CyVerACT: An Agentic Cypher Translation Workflow over Knowledge Graphs
papers.authors: Androna C.M., Mandilara I., Arkadopoulou E., Fotopoulou E., Zafeiropoulos A., Papavassiliou S.
papers.abstract: Question Answering (QA) over Knowledge Graphs (KGs) has greatly benefited from the rapid growth of Large Language Models (LLMs), which enable the translation of natural language questions into Cypher queries. Most existing approaches rely on one-shot generation via in-context learning or on fine-tuning LLMs; however, both strategies often struggle to generate accurate or executable queries, particularly when dealing with complex or unfamiliar graph schemas. To address these limitations, in this work we propose CyVerACT, an agentic workflow for Text-to-Cypher generation that empowers LLMs with execution- and schema-aware feedback mechanisms. CyVerACT leverages CyVer, a software tool that evaluates Cypher queries in terms of syntax validity and semantic compliance with respect to a specific KG schema, and detects their points of failure. The system customizes the input graph schema based on the input question and iteratively refines the generated queries taking advantage of the error metadata from CyVer to guide subsequent LLM generations. We evaluated and compared CyVerACT to existing single-shot generation and iterative refinement approaches in two publicly available Text-to-Cypher datasets of 2180 entries across various domains and complexities, using both foundational (e.g., GPT-4o, LLama-3) and fine-tuned state-of-the-art models. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed workflow significantly improves query correctness and execution success rates, achieving up to 52.7% gain in accuracy in terms of syntax validity and schema access, and 13.5% gain in exact match.

papers.title: Disentangled graph recommendation via dynamic long and short-term intent modeling
papers.authors: Wang J., Wang J., Jin D.
papers.abstract: User decision-making behavior is driven by multiple latent intents. These intents not only reflect user preferences but are also jointly influenced by long-term interests and short-term demands. However, in real-world scenarios, user intents evolve with changes in both time and environment. Existing disentanglement recommendation methods neglect the dynamic characteristic, making it difficult to effectively model the time-varying nature of user intent. Thus, we propose a disentanglement graph recommendation model based on long and short-term intent modeling(DGRLS), aiming to cope with the challenge of dynamic intent modeling. Specifically, DGRLS models user preferences across two dimensions: i) For short-term modeling, dynamic intent routing mechanism is introduced to capture the hierarchical relationships among multi-intent features and to optimize immediate intent through a decay time factor mechanism. ii) For long-term modeling, DGRLS analyzes users’ historical behavioral data employing a large language model, and integrated with a transformer architecture to accurately represent long-term interests. It is worth mentioning that, unlike existing approaches that employ hypergraphs or transformer to model long-term user behavioral preferences, DGRLS models the distribution of users’ dynamic intentions based on modal information in the semantic space. Extensive experiments on three public datasets show that the method is effective, which provides a new perspective for actively understanding modal information for user intent representation.
papers.keywords_json: ["Disentangled representation learning", "Dynamic intent learning", "Graph recommendation", "Large language model"]

papers.title: MFC4POI: Multi-factor collaboration for next point-of-interest recommendation using large language models
papers.authors: Song Y., Xu W., Liu L., Tiwari P., Tian G., Xie Q., Peng M.
papers.abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation aims to predict the next location a user will visit based on historical behavioral data. Given their strong natural language understanding and reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly introduced into next POI recommendation, as conventional methods are limited by their numerical representations, which often obscure the inherent semantic information embedded in contextual features However, LLM-based approaches struggle to effectively comprehend multiple factors holistically and express them in natural language. To address this issue, we propose Multi-Factor Collaboration for Next POI Recommendation (MFC4POI), a pretraining and fine-tuning framework that reformulates the next POI recommendation task as a question-answering problem. It leverages the strong comprehension and reasoning capabilities of LLMs to analyze user’s current behavior based on historical trajectories, and real time on-site situation, including the dynamic preferences and nearby geographic information in natural language. Due to the inherent limitations of LLMs in accurately modeling temporal and geographical information, MFC4POI introduces an intent identification agent to capture users’ dynamic preferences based on Spatio-temporal Intent-based Knowledge Graph (STIKG). It alleviates the weak spatial reasoning capability of LLMs while providing clear reasoning paths that make the recommendations more intuitive and coherent. To further improve understanding of users’s real-time on-site situation, MFC4POI integrates geographic information with dynamic preferences by providing nearby POIs that align with these dynamic preferences, thereby further enhancing LLMs’ performance. Experiments on three real-world datasets, containing up to 4000 users and 405000 check-ins, show that MFC4POI consistently outperforms strong baselines. Specifically, it achieves better performance than most baselines on Acc@1 and surpasses all baselines on Acc@5 and Acc@10 across all datasets.

papers.title: Adaptive model selection and ensemble via spatiotemporal graph-guided expert routing
papers.authors: Wang L., Cheng S., Lu F.
papers.abstract: Ensemble learning has shown strong potential for spatiotemporal inference by integrating multiple base models to improve accuracy and robustness. However, existing methods often rely on fixed sets of base models and localized ensemble strategies, limiting their adaptability to dynamic data patterns and global spatiotemporal correlations. To address this, we propose an adaptive ensemble framework that dynamically selects and fuses multiple models under varied spatiotemporal conditions. First, a graph-based module is presented to encode the spatial relationships among sensor nodes and the temporal dynamics of their time series into unified context embeddings. Second, an adaptive routing mechanism is designed to compute context-dependent response scores to guide model selection. Finally, a context-specific ensemble strategy aggregates model outputs using weights derived from these scores. Experiments on traffic flow, traffic speed, and air quality datasets show that the proposed framework achieves consistently competitive and often better performance than both mainstream ensemble methods and recent dynamic graph models, reducing inference errors by up to 2.1%-4.7% while using 11%-60% fewer parameters and maintaining comparable inference efficiency. Further interpretability analysis confirms that the framework effectively captures spatiotemporal correlations and performance heterogeneity, thereby enabling adaptive model selection and fusion in response to local contextual variations.

papers.title: Graph-driven knowledge stream method for knowledge management in vertical domain large language models: Case study on pit engineering application
papers.authors: Xia Z., Zhong B., Zhang S., Zhao T.
papers.abstract: Embedding professional knowledge is crucial during developing vertical domain large language models (LLMs). While rapid progress of LLM coexists with barriers to professional knowledge access. Such coexistence highlights the need for effective knowledge management during vertical domain LLM development, yet existing research seldom focuses on this. To solve this gap, we conduct three works: (1) Based on insights of knowledge structural representation, we propose a graph-driven knowledge stream method that models knowledge enabling activities as measurable flows; (2) a knowledge graph (KG)-anchored evaluation protocol is proposed to quantify graph coverage, constraint consistency, hallucination rate, and retention for evaluating knowledge enablement; (3) we integrate graph-anchored evaluation, LLM-graph interaction pipeline, federated learning (FL), and blockchain as graph-driven vertical domain LLM development framework (GVLDF). GVLDF enables knowledge aggregation and reuse, efficacy auditing, and continual optimization. In a foundation pit engineering case study (58,451 tokens fine-tuned vertical domain LLM), GVLDF improved graph coverage from 0.712 to 0.889, raised constraint consistency from 94.3% to 98.1%, and reduced hallucination rate from 0.220 to 0.063, while maintaining retention above 0.87. These findings show that structural anchoring systematically enhances reliability, compliance, and sustainability in vertical LLM development. Our research provides a reliable theory and solution for sustainable enablement and robust deployment of vertical domain LLM.

papers.title: H-ProtoRAG: A hierarchical prototype-based retrieval-augmented framework for multilingual CPC patent classification and prior-art retrieval
papers.authors: Elmi Z.
papers.abstract: Patent documents are long, multi-label, and hierarchically structured texts, which makes joint Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) assignment and prior-art retrieval particularly challenging in multilingual settings. Existing patent classifiers and retrievers typically treat sections and tasks in isolation and often under-specify how retrieved evidence should influence final label decisions and calibration. We propose H-ProtoRAG, a hierarchical prototype-based, retrieval-augmented framework that couples dual encoders with section-aware pooling over titles, abstracts, and claims, a claim–evidence alignment module trained on PatentMatch, and a multi-loss objective combining cross-entropy, supervised contrastive, prototype, hierarchical, retrieval, and NLI terms. For claim–evidence supervision, we adopt a fixed multilingual NLI teacher, namely XLM-R fine-tuned on XNLI, as the default pseudo-labeling mechanism; token-overlap rules are retained only as a lexical ablation to quantify the gap between surface-form heuristics and semantically grounded pseudo-labeling. Using 1.2M Turkish/English patents from the BigQuery CPC corpus together with BIGPATENT, PatentMatch, CLEF-IP 2010, MAREC, and PatTR, we evaluate H-ProtoRAG under in-domain, cross-source, and multilingual scenarios. On Turkish CPC classification, H-ProtoRAG improves Micro-F1 from 45.3% (PatentBERT) to 55.3% and Hierarchical-F1 from 55.0% to 63.7%; on English, it raises Micro-F1 from 52.0–53.8% to 58.6%. On CLEF-IP 2010 prior-art retrieval, our hybrid dense–sparse retriever with cross-encoder re-ranking increases nDCG@10 from 0.212 (BM25) to 0.301 and Precision@1 from 0.41 to 0.60 while maintaining Recall@50 at 69.4%. The same retrieval stack is further used to construct teacher-supervised evidence signals that recalibrate classification scores under hierarchical CPC ambiguity. Calibration is also improved, with Expected Calibration Error reduced from 12.4% to 6.1% and top-5% prediction precision increased from 71% to 85%, supporting more reliable multilingual patent analytics.

papers.title: LLM-assisted fake news detection with adaptive boosting framework incorporating contrastive learning
papers.authors: Yin S., Wang Y., Hou D., An W., Gao C., Li X., Wang Z.
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of digital technologies, the widespread spread of fake news on social media platforms may threaten social stability. Existing methods often use small models as feature extractors for news content, relying on the inherent pattern differences between true and false news as the basis for fake news detection. However, smaller models cannot perceive latent background information in news content. Additionally, fake news is much less prevalent than true news on real social platforms, which may lead to issues with data collection imbalance of true and false labels. These challenges may limit the effectiveness of existing detection methods. Therefore, we propose a Large Language Model-assisted Fake News Detection method with Adaptive Boosting, denoted as LFND-AB. Specifically, we first employ the large language model to generate analyses of the truthfulness and falseness of news text, which contains background information about the news. We then design an explainable base learner for fake news detection that utilizes contrastive learning to align the similarity between the news text and the corresponding generated analyses to obtain higher-quality fused representations. Furthermore, we design an adaptive ensemble boosting framework based on the base learner. This framework adjusts the weights of misclassified samples to improve the detection performance in the next base learner, thereby optimizing the model’s ability to handle label imbalance. The comprehensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that both the proposed base learner and LFND-AB outperform State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) methods. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/cgao-comp/FEND.
papers.keywords_json: ["Fake news detection", "Large language model", "Social network", "Text analysis"]

papers.title: R&D partner recommendation and network prediction using patent data: A deep learning approach
papers.authors: Wang J., Chen H.W., Shih Y.H.
papers.abstract: R&D partner selection is often guided by expert judgment, and prior patent-based studies rarely integrate bibliometric, semantic, and network evidence in a unified predictive framework. This study develops a deep learning approach that fuses patent bibliometric indicators, SBERT-based textual embeddings, and network link prediction features to recommend R&D partners and anticipate future collaboration networks. Using USPTO patent applications in the self-driving vehicle domain (2018 to 2023), we construct a dataset of 23,796 patents, including 5237 collaborative patents. The fused model achieves 83.33% precision, 66.67% F1, and 57.55% PR-AUC, improving F1 and PR-AUC by 3.18 and 5.18 percentage points over the strongest single-feature baseline. It also outperforms classical machine-learning baselines, raising PR-AUC by 20.58 percentage points relative to XGBoost. SHAP-based analysis indicates complementary contributions from bibliometric, semantic-textual, and network signals, supporting shortlists for both exploitation-oriented and exploration-oriented collaboration strategies. Beyond partner recommendations, the model offers forward-looking insights into network evolution, indicating a continued tendency toward denser and more interconnected collaboration clusters in this sector.

papers.title: An All-in-One Quality Assessment Agent for 4D digital human: Bridging talking heads and animated human
papers.authors: Zhou Y., Zhang Z., Wen F., Xu L., Zhang Y., Zhou Y., Cao J., Shi Y., Liu X., Min X., Wang Y., Zhai G.
papers.abstract: As advancements in 4D digital human (4DDH) technology continue to progress rapidly, ensuring and evaluating its quality has become a significant concern. To support the ongoing development of 4DDH and enhance user experience, we conduct a comprehensive quality assessment of 4DDH content. Specifically, we introduce H4DQA, the large-scale 4DDH quality assessment dataset, comprising 3220 4DDH samples categorized into two groups: Talking Head and Animated Human. Furthermore, the dataset incorporates model-based, motion-based, and quality of experience (QoE) distortions to enhance diversity and robustness in quality assessment. Building upon the H4DQA dataset, we develop an All-in-One Quality Assessment Agent (A3gent) for 4DDHs, leveraging a multimodal large language model (MLLM). This framework provides an effective, reliable, and efficient objective quality assessment method for 4DDHs. The proposed A3gent integrates visual, phonetic, and posture features, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on the H4DQA dataset. Our approach offers valuable insights for advancing digital human technology and establishing standardized quality assessment protocols.

papers.title: MLAFormer: Multi-scale transformer with local convolutional auto-correlation and pre-training for time series forecasting
papers.authors: Jin Y., Gao M., Tang J., Fan W., Yang Y., An J.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based models have achieved strong performance in long-term time series forecasting, yet they often struggle to jointly model short-term local patterns and long-range dependencies under a unified representation, especially when temporal dynamics vary across different resolutions. To address this challenge, we propose MLAFormer, a multi-scale encoder-decoder framework for long-sequence forecasting. MLAFormer learns temporal representations across multiple resolutions through a cross multi-scale architecture, enabling information exchange between fine-grained and coarse-grained temporal features. In addition, we propose a Local Convolutional Auto-correlation mechanism to enhance local contextual modeling while capturing periodic dependencies efficiently. To further improve representation quality, we incorporate self-supervised pre-training within the encoder-decoder framework and investigate different masking strategies for time series reconstruction. Extensive experiments on nine benchmark datasets demonstrate that MLAFormer consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods in long-term forecasting. On average, MLAFormer reduces MAE by 7.4% compared with the recent advanced model, with an additional 3.0% improvement through pre-training.

papers.title: Fair client selection for multi-task federated learning in mobile edge networks
papers.authors: Su L., Guo J., Liu J., Liu X.
papers.abstract: Multi-task federated learning (FL) in mobile edge networks faces significant challenges due to the coexistence of heterogeneous tasks, dynamic client states, and limited computational resources. Most existing client selection methods often assume a single-task scenario with prior knowledge of client conditions, making them unsuitable for real-world multi-task training. Moreover, a critical issue is fairness: if resource-abundant devices are consistently favored, weaker clients may be excluded, leading to biased global models and lower training performance. To bridge this gap, we propose multi-task client selection MTC, a novel online algorithm that reformulates the selection process as a multi-agent multi-armed bandit (MAMAB) problem with proportional fairness constraints. MTC operates in rounds, each comprising four stages-exploration, mapping, exploitation, and rounding-enabling it to learn client performance while ensuring efficient and fair resource allocation. Theoretically, MTC can achieve both sub-linear regret and computational efficiency. Empirically, extensive experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that MTC not only improves accuracy by up to 2% to 26% over state-of-the-art baselines (EffI-FL, EMAFL, Fair-CFL, and FedProx), but also significantly enhances fairness-ensuring that even resource-constrained devices contribute to training. These results highlight the practical value of fair client selection for robust FL in real-world mobile edge networks.

papers.title: How to teach and forget: Towards cross-modal semantic consistency for entity alignment
papers.authors: Wang C., Miao C., Hu P., Wang W., Bao F.
papers.abstract: Multimodal Entity Alignment (MEA) aims to match identical entities across Multimodal Knowledge Graphs (MMKGs) by integrating complementary information from different modalities, such as visual and structure. In practice, MEA is complicated by two issues. Within a single MMKG, different modalities describing the same entity may not align well semantically. Across different MMKGs, the same entity may be associated with inconsistent or incomplete modality information, even within the same modality type. To address these challenges, we propose TeFo, a novel framework designed to enhance cross-modal semantic consistency by Teaching and Forgetting. Specifically, we introduce the Adaptive Modality Distillation module to teach. It aggregates semantic signals from multiple modalities to construct a modality-aware teacher representation. This teacher helps align each single-modality student toward a unified semantic space, which in turn alleviates inter-graph heterogeneity. Furthermore, we design the Gated Adversarial Alignment module to forget. It combines a gated feature selector and a modality discriminator trained with gradient reversal to reduce modality-specific variation. This encourages TeFo to rely less on modality-specific cues, and implicitly improves its robustness to modality asymmetry. Extensive experiments on nine public datasets show that TeFo significantly surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods, yielding absolute gains of 1.9%-2.3% in Hits@1 and 1.4%-2.4% in MRR. Our code is available at https://github.com/wonderCS1213/TeFo.
papers.keywords_json: ["Knowledge graph", "Multi-modal entity alignment", "Multi-modal learning"]

papers.title: CTJANet: A class-task joint-aware network for enhanced few-shot image classification
papers.authors: Sun Z., Wang M., Zhang X., Guo P.
papers.abstract: Few-shot image classification remains challenging due to the difficulty of recognizing novel categories from limited labeled samples. While recent methods employ information-aware strategies, they often depend on a single type of perceptual cue, missing the benefits of integrating multiple perspectives. To overcome this limitation, we propose a CTJANet (Class-Task Joint-Aware Network), which jointly leverages class-aware and task-aware cues for enhanced feature representation. Furthermore, we introduce a Task Adaptive-Aware Module (TAAM) that dynamically extracts task-specific embeddings through task-aware functions, improving adaptability to diverse tasks. Extensive experiments show that CTJANet outperforms the baseline FewTURE by significant margins: +5.29% (1-shot) and +3.74% (5-shot) on mini-ImageNet, +4.98% (1-shot) and +4.12% (5-shot) on tiered-ImageNet, +3.00% (1-shot) and +1.54% (5-shot) on CIFAR-FS, and +3.90% (1-shot) and +3.58% (5-shot) on FC100. Ablation studies also confirm the superiority of CTJANet, maintaining high classification accuracy and strong generalization. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/xiaozhugongqang/ZitWMY.

papers.title: Extracting policy attention from Chinese texts: An LLM-enhanced dynamic topic modeling approach for the “Dual Carbon” agenda
papers.authors: Guo Y., Yu S., Fu M., Jiang C.
papers.abstract: Extracting dynamic policy attention from large-scale Chinese policy texts remains challenging due to limitations in semantic representation and temporal modeling. This study proposes a Chinese-Prompt Dynamic Topic Model (CPDTM) that integrates Chinese pretrained language models with large language model–based prompt engineering to systematically link governmental attention allocation to governance outcomes. Taking 3056 “dual carbon” policy documents issued between October 2020 and June 2024 as an example, CPDTM achieves the best performance in topic quality. Our experiments identify the evolving policy attention in four key domains: ecological and meteorological development, green and low-carbon governance, industrial energy conservation and emission reduction, and technological innovation and development, showing a significant shift toward green and low-carbon governance. Furthermore, an autoregressive distributed lag model (ARDL) indicates that a 1% increase in long-run policy attention is associated with carbon emissions reductions of 0.5%, 0.3%, 0.2%, and 1.4% across these domains, while short-run effects vary substantially. Additionally, policy attention reduces carbon emissions through three primary channels: environmental governance constraints, green technology innovation, and industrial structure adjustment. This study contributes by (1) advancing dynamic topic modeling through LLM-enhanced prompting for large-scale Chinese policy texts, (2) uncovering the temporal evolution of “dual carbon” policy attention, and (3) providing empirical evidence on how information embedded in policy texts translates into emission outcomes, offering insights for policy optimization and sustainable governance.

papers.title: Legacy Learning Strategy Based on Few-Shot Font Generation Models for Automatic Text Design
papers.authors: Kim Y., Jeong S.C., Kim D., Sim S.
papers.abstract: Text design plays a vital role in enhancing user experience and maintaining visual coherence across digital platforms. However, for languages containing thousands of glyphs, creating new fonts remains costly and labor-intensive. Few-shot font generation (FFG) has emerged as a promising approach that synthesizes unseen glyphs from a small number of reference samples. Nevertheless, over 5–10% of glyphs must still be manually produced, limiting scalability. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a plug-and-play legacy learning strategy that enhances both stylistic diversity and structural stability. The model-agnostic method performs iterative cross-font fine-tuning, progressively aligning the pretrained models' style representation toward a legacy-centric embedding space while introducing a content preservation loss to constrain geometric deformation and maintain glyph integrity. The proposed strategy was applied to five state-of-the-art FFG models and evaluated on large-scale Korean, Chinese and Thai font sets. Experimental results based on Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) similarity show that the generated glyphs gradually diverged from the original font distribution while converging toward the legacy font distribution, achieving stylistic variety with structural coherence. In addition, quantitative assessments of structural preservation and readability (Dice similarity, Chamfer distance, and OCR) confirm geometric stability without structural collapse. Cross-language and multilingual generalization was further verified, and a user study with 70 participants (experts and nonexperts) achieved average usability scores above 4.5/5. These results highlight legacy learning as an efficient and scalable strategy for automated, high-quality font generation in multilingual digital content environments.

papers.title: Dualmark: A novel dual watermarking approach for large language models
papers.authors: Qiang Z., Hao J., Qiang J., Zhu Y., Zhang C., Liu Y., Li W.
papers.abstract: Watermarking, which embeds imperceptible yet machine-detectable patterns into generated text, has emerged as a leading solution for detecting machine-generated content. While green-red watermarking methods embed detectable signals by biasing a “green” token subset, they remain vulnerable to paraphrasing attacks and context shifts: green tokens can be replaced, and edits to preceding tokens can disrupt the green-red partition. To address these limitations, we introduce DualMark, a novel ensemble-based dual-watermarking framework that employs an ensemble-inspired approach to embed two independent green-red watermarks using separate context windows and partitioning strategies. During generation, DualMark applies a tiered bias strategy, strongest to tokens in the intersection of both green lists while also biasing tokens unique to each list. Detection succeeds if either watermark yields a statistically significant signal. DualMark integrates seamlessly with existing watermarking schemes and incurs minimal overhead. Extensive experiments across various adversarial scenarios demonstrate that DualMark maintains text quality while substantially outperforming single-watermark baselines: it improves detection AUROC by over 11% under severe word-deletion attacks and doubles the true positive rate (TP@1%) against adaptive baselines under heavy paraphrasing, all while incurring only a 5% increase in generation latency.

papers.title: Network infrastructure construction and digital innovation resilience: Evidence from Broadband China policy
papers.authors: Jiang W., Jiang N., Yu D.
papers.abstract: We use data from 271 prefecture-level cities in China from 2011 to 2023 and treat the Broadband China policy as a quasi-natural experiment to examine how network infrastructure construction influences digital innovation resilience. The results indicate that network infrastructure construction raises digital innovation resilience. This conclusion remains valid after instrumental variable estimation and a series of robustness tests. This effect is particularly pronounced in cities characterized by high traditional infrastructure construction, low intellectual property protection, and strong government support for science and education. Mechanism analysis suggests that resilience is enhanced mainly through narrowing the digital divide and fostering innovation collaboration, while the mediating role of digital finance is not supported. This study adds to the literature on digital innovation resilience and offers policy insights for promoting network infrastructure construction in a sustainable way.
